headline: Shrenik Limited: Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process initiated
sum: Shrenik Limited has been admitted into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. The company has disclosed the constitution of a Committee of Creditors (CoC) to the NSE.
implication: CIRP admission triggers a 180-day (extendable to 270-day) moratorium on creditor action; the CoC must approve any resolution plan or recommend liquidation, making insolvency counsel and restructuring strategy central to stakeholder outcomes.
detail: Shrenik Limited, an industrial company, has formally entered CIRP following admission by the adjudicating authority (NCLT). Constitution of the Committee of Creditors has been disclosed to the stock exchange as mandated under IBC and listing regulations. The CoC will evaluate resolution plans or recommend liquidation within the statutory timeline. The company's operations remain subject to moratorium provisions.

framework.note: Central: definition and admission criteria for CIRP; triggers 180-day (extendable to 270-day) resolution window.
Central: Committee of Creditors formation, composition, and voting thresholds (66% for plan approval).
Central: moratorium on institution or continuation of suits, criminal proceedings and recovery actions against the corporate debtor.
Central: resolution plan submission, evaluation and approval process; plan must be feasible and viable.

framework.ref: SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR) Regulations, 2015, Regulation 30 & Schedule III
framework.note: Central: mandatory disclosure to stock exchange of material corporate action, including CIRP admission and CoC constitution.
Central: distribution of resolution plan consideration; waterfall priority among creditor classes.
Procedural: NCLT adjudication on CIRP admission and resolution plan approval; appeal rights under Section 61.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporate Persons) Regulations, 2016 (as amended 2020, 2023, 2024)
framework.note: Amended: CoC conduct, information utility integration, pre-packaged insolvency (PPI) and fast-track processes; review current regulations.

conditions: Admission by NCLT adjudicating authority under Section 7, 9 or 10 of IBC 2016
Constitution of Committee of Creditors comprising financial creditors (by value weighted) and operational creditors
66% CoC approval threshold required for resolution plan adoption
Completion within 180 days (extendable by another 90 days to 270 days maximum)
approvals: CoC approval of resolution plan (if plan proceeds)
NCLT approval of resolution plan (final gate)
structure.novel: Company has disclosed CoC constitution to stock exchange in real-time compliance with SEBI LODR and IBC procedural transparency requirements.

triggers.note: Entire CIRP framework applies; any corporate debtor with default of ₹1 cr or more may be admitted on creditor/debtor application.
Listing company must disclose CIRP admission and CoC constitution to stock exchange as material corporate action.

triggers.law: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India Regulations, 2016 (as amended)
triggers.note: CoC conduct, information system, resolution professional duties and timelines are prescribed; recent amendments (2023–24) allow faster processes and pre-packaged options.
